construct: TMPRSS15 encodes enteropeptidase (enterokinase), a brush-border serine protease of the proximal small intestine. Enteropeptidase initiates pancreatic protease activation by cleaving trypsinogen to active trypsin; trypsin then activates additional pancreatic zymogens.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Biallelic TMPRSS15 loss with infantile protein malabsorption identifies enteropeptidase deficiency; the direct brush-border reaction is cleavage of trypsinogen to trypsin.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidase activation are downstream trypsin-mediated events, pepsinogen activation occurs in the stomach, and lipase-colipase interaction is not the enteropeptidase reaction.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The lead asks for the zymogen step most directly impaired, which uniquely distinguishes trypsinogen activation from downstream protease-cascade consequences.
